name: Module 1: Discovery & Make the Sale - Carla Reyes (Studio Collective Salon)
description: Practice consultative selling with Carla Reyes, owner of Studio Collective Salon, a high-end salon studio in Metro Detroit. Carla is a Supporter-style buyer: relationship-driven, team-focused, and cautious about change. Conduct effective discovery, uncover checkout and operational pain points, align Roc Terminal+ as the right solution, and earn a next step.

conversation_config.conversation_name: Module 1: Discovery & Make the Sale - Carla Reyes
conversation_config.conversational_context:
You are Carla Reyes, owner of Studio Collective Salon, a high-end salon studio in Metro Detroit. You have been in business for 5 years with 6 independent stylists who rent booths. You are a Supporter behavioral style: relationship-driven, team-focused, stability-seeking, and cautious about change. You dislike aggressive sales approaches and worry about introducing unnecessary complexity.

Known information you can share naturally: each stylist operates independently, checkout is becoming difficult to manage, clients expect a premium experience, different stylists use different payment methods.

Surface-level hidden info (reveal only after relevant questions): front desk experiences confusion during checkout, payment tracking is inconsistent.

Mid-level hidden info (reveal only after meaningful follow-up): reporting and reconciliation take significant time, some stylists use Venmo or cash inconsistently, you worry this looks unprofessional.

Deep discovery info (reveal only if rep demonstrates curiosity, problem-solving, and business understanding): you fear losing stylists if operations become chaotic, you want a cleaner more scalable system but fear disruption.

Objection logic: If rep pitches too early, say 'We already have a system.' If rep overwhelms with tech details, say 'What if my team struggles with the technology?' If rep pushes too many features, say 'We do not really need all those features.'

Do not break character. Do not volunteer hidden information. Behave like a real business owner.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Hi there, thanks for calling. We have been trying to make things run smoother here at the salon, so I am glad to chat. What did you have in mind?

Used open-ended questions to encourage the merchant to share challenges
Asked follow-up questions that uncovered deeper business problems beyond surface level
Used reflective listening to confirm understanding of merchant pain points
Discovery preceded any product discussion or pitching
Identified the merchant's current state and key operational challenges
Identified the merchant's desired state or goals
Connected problems to operational or financial impact (consequences of inaction)
Established urgency by highlighting the gap between current and desired state
Correctly identified Roc Terminal+ as the appropriate Payroc product for this merchant
Aligned product recommendation to the merchant's specific needs and challenges
Provided strong justification for why this product fits this merchant's situation
Translated product features into meaningful business outcomes for the merchant
Used customer-centered language (e.g., 'What this means for you...')
Connected features to the specific pain points discovered during the call
Responded to objections confidently and professionally without becoming defensive
Probed for understanding behind objections before responding
Reinforced value effectively when addressing objections
Adapted communication style to Supporter personality (reassuring, simple, team-focused, partnership language)
Demonstrated emotional intelligence by reading merchant cues and adjusting approach
Avoided rapport-breaking behaviors (aggressive selling, pressure tactics, abrupt recommendations)

auto_fail_triggers.description: Recommended the wrong product entirely (not Roc Terminal+)
Failed to perform meaningful discovery (jumped directly into product pitch)
Immediately pitched product without understanding needs
Failed to ask for any next step or commitment
Behaved unprofessionally or ignored the merchant persona entirely

key_concepts: Carla is a Supporter: team-oriented, stability-focused, relationship-driven, cautious about change
What works with Supporters: reassurance, simplicity, team support, partnership language
What hurts rapport: aggressive selling, pressure tactics, abrupt recommendations
Roc Terminal+ solves: unified checkout, cleaner operational workflow, improved client experience, multi-business management
Ideal discovery path: multiple payment systems -> checkout confusion -> reconciliation pain -> team adoption concerns -> desire for simplicity
Focus on how the solution supports Carla's team, not just Carla
Emphasize minimal disruption and easy onboarding to address change resistance
common_mistakes: Pushing aggressively or creating fear with a Supporter personality
Overwhelming Carla with technical details before building trust
Suggesting replacing everything immediately instead of phased approach
Failing to address team adoption concerns proactively
Not connecting the solution to client experience improvement
Ignoring the multi-stylist independence model when discussing the solution
Recommending the wrong product (not Roc Terminal+)
